title: Durable provider-delivery receipt: a host-dispatched prompt records a delivery identity and an acknowledged hand-off, so an ambiguous send is never replayed blindly or called delivered
outcome: Durable provider-delivery receipt: a host-dispatched prompt records a delivery identity and an acknowledged hand-off, so an ambiguous send is never replayed blindly or called delivered
acceptance: For such a prompt, the host durably records a write-ahead hand-off attempt (prompt id, transcript message id, attempt number and the runtime attempt key), acknowledged before the runtime is called. It records acceptance on the runtime's first positive acknowledgement: Claude command_lifecycle queued/started for the attempt uuid, or its unique replay echo; Codex's turn/start response or turn/started; for ACP, the session/prompt response. It records a definite rejection only when the hand-off provably never reached the runtime. The prompt's delivery disposition is one of pending, handing-off, accepted, rejected or ambiguous, and is exposed on the wire.

After a restart, an accepted attempt reads as delivered and is never replayed. A handing-off attempt without acceptance reads as ambiguous: it is never replayed and never called delivered. A rejected attempt may be re-queued only under a new prompt id bound to a new prerequisite, which the old acknowledgement cannot satisfy. Tests cover a restart before the write-ahead commit, after it, after acceptance and after rejection, plus a Codex timeout and a Claude write error (both ambiguous).

No new poller, watchdog, timer, sleep or enlarged timeout is introduced; dispositions advance only on existing runtime events, acknowledgements and boot reconciliation. The ACP gap (no acceptance signal before the end-of-turn response) is documented in the feature doc, and nothing reports such a prompt delivered earlier.
The full gate passes on the exact committed tree.
